title: Preventing double-credit and drift during tenant quota epoch handoffs
creator: Alyssa Carter
description:
Background: We regularly see tenant quota accounting drift when tenants move between reserved pools or when epoch boundaries (daily/monthly/rolling windows) intersect tenant-specific timezone offsets and DST transitions. Symptoms include transient double-credit, lost credits during handoffs, and over-deductions after lease migrations. This is especially visible for Reserved capacity customers who have lease-based reservations and for tenants with non-UTC billing anchors.

Problem statement: The current reset pipeline applies epoch resets per-reservation and then reconciles tenant-level usage. Race windows exist when: (1) a tenant lease is moved between reserved pools around an epoch boundary; (2) host-level epoch rollovers overlap with tenant-local daily resets (timezone/DST); (3) quota reconciliation jobs run concurrently with live invoicing snapshots. These races cause either granting extra tokens (double-credit) or failing to carry forward remaining balance (lost credit).

Goals: 1) Eliminate double-credit windows during lease handoffs and pool rebinding. 2) Ensure deterministic tenant-level balances across timezone-aware epoch boundaries. 3) Provide clear audit trails and revert-safe reconciliation when a mis-credit is detected. 4) Maintain near-zero customer-visible disruption and keep compute cost reasonable.

Proposed approach: A multi-part engineering solution that is backwards-compatible and incrementally deployable: 
- Anchor epochs to a single canonical timeline per-tenant (billing_anchor). The billing_anchor is either UTC-midnight, tenant-accounting-tier anchor, or a custom tenant timezone anchor. All reset operations for that tenant derive offsets from billing_anchor so DST shifts are predictable.
- Introduce lease tombstones with versioned epoch pointers. When a lease is moved between pools, write a tombstone record (lease_id, old_pool, new_pool, effective_epoch_id, version_nonce) and make reset/reconcile idempotent by comparing epoch pointers.
- Two-phase reset protocol: (A) mark-phase: create a transient snapshot and write intended debit/credit operations into a per-tenant ledger with epoch_id and tombstone_nonce; (B) commit-phase: atomically apply ledger entries after cross-checking that no conflicting tombstone/version changes happened during mark. If conflict, abort and run deterministic merge.
- Grace tokens: for lease handoffs that occur within a configurable handoff_window (default 5 minutes), grant a conservatively-estimated grace token allowance to prevent immediate over-deduction, then reconcile exact usage in the next commit window.
- Deterministic reconciliation job that runs post-epoch (within 10 minutes) to detect mismatches between ledger and billing snapshot and either auto-correct or open a review ticket for manual resolution depending on confidence level. Corrections are appended to the tenant audit log with before/after balance and sign-off fields.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: UI work in Console, pricing/offline billing pipeline changes. This ticket focuses on runtime quota semantics, edge-case reconciliation logic, and auditability for reserved capacity leases.

Why this is different: Existing tickets focused on per-epoch resets or lease checkpoint reconciliation in isolation. This work targets the intersection of lease handoffs, timezone-anchored epochs, and reconciliation semantics to remove a class of rare but high-severity customer bill discrepancies.
acceptance_criteria: No double-credit incidents reproducible in synthetic handoff tests covering: pool move at epoch boundary, DST forward/back shifts, and tenant-custom anchor offsets.
Unit + integration tests that simulate tombstone/version conflicts and show deterministic merge outcomes.
A 10-minute post-epoch reconciliation job that produces an audit log entry for every tenant with modifications required and auto-corrects low-confidence mismatches with metrics recorded.
End-to-end e2e test that migrates a reserved lease between pools during a simulated monthly reset and asserts tenant balance invariants.
Documentation page (internal) describing billing_anchor semantics and operational runbook for manual reconciliation.
A migration plan with a canary rollout and telemetry dashboards (token-level diffs, reconciliation rate, number of tombstone conflicts) instrumented.

2026-03-06 Diego Martinez: Performance note: mark+commit phases add ~2ms median latency on quota check path when enabled. We should gate feature behind config for reserved pools and run a canary. Also added telemetry for commit conflicts: metric quota.commit_conflicts.count
